commit_subject: (screen-flagged) Time-bound: Idaho pilot bounded to 2026, drops source-certified parity claim and relabels 2026 indexed amounts as caller-supplied projections.
description: bounds the projected/caller-supplied scaffold through 2026, adds dense floor/threshold fixtures, explicitly retains the official-source HOLD/no-parity boundary

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: All three versions opened at 2026-01-01 with no effective_to, so the module asserted that a configuration built entirely on unverified 2026 projections (the indexed no-tax threshold and the post-step rate) was valid for every period from 2026 onward, even though the cited section 63-3024 directs the State Tax Commission to reindex the threshold annually and the pinned corpus holds no source certifying any of those year-specific values.
triage.triage_notes: Single module in the commit. The only semantic delta is three identical '+ effective_to: 2026-12-31' hunks (one per rule version); the rest of the module diff is rationale/summary prose that removes the pre-fix claims that 'the operative 2026 rate and threshold are the indexed values PolicyEngine projects', the literal '$4,920 single / $9,840 joint at 2026' and '5.3-per-cent' figures, and the 'comparable to PolicyEngine id_income_tax to the cent' parity assertion. Formulas, inputs, outputs, entity, and citation paths are unchanged, so on its own the prose rewrite would be metadata/mechanical; the effective_to additions are what make this a period-scope correction. I read the cited provision through the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix): us-id/statute/63-3024 resolves to legislature site navigation chrome only, with fix_time_corpus_match = row_body_empty_at_corpus_ref, i.e. the corpus row carries no operative statutory text, which corroborates the module's new 'corpus does not yet contain a Tax Commission source certifying the operative 2026 indexed values' rationale and the withdrawal of the parity claim. Residual doubt on the classification: because every year-specific amount is a caller-supplied input rather than a literal, no source sentence is directly contradicted by the pre-fix formulas, so a reviewer could read the bounding as fail-closed scaffolding hygiene rather than a source disagreement; I kept 'fidelity' because the encoded version window claimed validity the module's own cited authority (annual reindexation, no certified source) cannot support, and PR #1017 names it as a 'period-boundary' gap. Companion test file gained five boundary fixtures in the same commit (test-side, not counted here). Follow-ups in the same PR but NOT in this commit: removal of the incorrect legacy us-id/statute/63-3022D citation/index edge (63-3022D is still listed in this commit's corpus_citation_paths), and a later head fed5817295 that deleted a stale Idaho pending-validation waiver block after CI failed with 'pending validation fingerprint evidence mismatch'.
triage.verifier_justification: The only meaning change is three added `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` lines; formulas, inputs, entity/period kind, proof atoms and citation paths are untouched, and the pre-fix module contains no year-specific literal at all — the threshold, both rates, the deduction subtraction and the exemption credit are all caller-supplied inputs, so nothing encoded goes stale in 2027. Resolving both cited paths through the fix commit's pinned toolchain returns only Idaho Legislature navigation chrome, with `"fix_time_corpus_match": "row_body_empty_at_corpus_ref"` at corpus ref 527a5be2, so the pinned corpus holds no operative text of 63-3024 that could make the open-ended window disagree with the source, and Idaho's single-rate structure has no 2026 sunset. The commit's own added rationale grounds the bound in corpus *absence* ("The corpus does not yet contain a Tax Commission source certifying the operative 2026 indexed values"), and the PR frames it as "Fail close 2026 state income-tax boundary modules" alongside withdrawal of an unsupported oracle-parity claim. That is a fail-closed governance/truthfulness scoping choice plus a provenance retraction, not a correction of encoded meaning against cited source text.
triage.verifier_quote:
+        corpus does not yet contain a Tax Commission source certifying the
+        operative 2026 indexed values, so every year-specific amount is a
+        declared caller-supplied projection: the filing-status no-tax threshold,
triage.verifier_notes: Refutation targets the classification, not the kind: if the corpus's convention is that an unbounded window on unverified-projection scaffolding is itself a period-truthfulness defect, then wrong_period_or_effective_date is the right kind and the first reader stands — my disagreement is whether any source-fidelity defect exists when the cited provision has no text in the pinned corpus. Verified facts for the reviewer: (1) module diff meaning change is exactly three `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` additions (rules[0..2].versions[0]); everything else is rationale/summary prose. (2) Pre-fix file (parent 07f5517d74) has zero numeric literals in any formula — all year-specific amounts arrive as `id_pit_pilot_supplied_*` inputs, so the post-2026 window could not produce a wrong number. (3) resolve_provision.py for us-id/statute/63-3024 and us-id/statute/63-3022D at commit 9d343d49a3 returns 956 chars of site navigation ("Senate Senate Leadership … How current is this law?") and reports row bodies empty at the toolchain corpus ref — no statutory rate, threshold, or effective-period text exists to be disagreed with. (4) Side effects worth a second look, both out of scope for this verdict: the bound now makes the module fail closed for 2027+ although the statutory single-rate mechanics continue (an under-claim with no statutory sunset), and the unchanged proof-atom excerpts ("5.3% of taxable income over $2,500, or over $5,000 for joint returns"; "a tax measured by Idaho taxable income") cannot be located in the resolved corpus body — a separate provenance issue this commit did not fix. (5) The same commit adds five 2026-period boundary fixtures (floor, ±$0.01 around the supplied threshold, credit floor) that exercise only caller-supplied mechanics; test additions do not bear on fidelity. If a reviewer prefers not to acquit outright, "unclear" is the next-best label; "mechanical" is wrong because version windows changed.
